text:
Emma S. (Support): Incoming from Acme — they need streaming chat that supports function/tool calls producing structured JSON outputs, plus a reliable non-streaming fallback when their webhook is slow. They want logs showing partial outputs. Ticket ACME-4567: https://acme.atlassian.net/browse/ACME-4567

Jake L. (Sales): This could be an expansion (~$400k ARR). Need ETA and major blockers. :money_with_wings:

Maria P. (Product): Quick clarifying q's: 1) Is "structured outputs" strict JSON-schema enforcement or just function_call-style args? 2) On fallback: should we buffer until webhook returns or emit a `call_started` marker and continue tokens? 3) SLA: per-request latency or guaranteed delivery of function result?

Emma S. (Support): Customer example pasted: 
stream: token "Hi"
stream: token " there"
stream: function_call {"name":"lookup_customer","arguments":{"id":"123"}}
They said: if webhook is slow, they want either continued intermediate tokens or at least an event indicating call in progress.

Olivia R. (Solutions Eng): We can add `call_started` and `call_finished` events. To stream tokens while webhook runs we'd need an async/non-blocking toolcall mode: queue the call, emit placeholder tokens, then emit `call_finished` and result when it returns. Could be opt-in via header like `Prefer: non-blocking-toolcalls`.

Kai W. (Eng): Current runtime blocks on toolcall response and pauses token streaming. Non-blocking requires: 1) durable queue for call requests, 2) markers in stream, 3) merge logic when call result arrives. Concerns: token ordering, KV cache alignment, backpressure, cost.

Maria P. (Product): Draft scope: Phase 1 = token streaming + explicit `call_started`/`call_finished` markers (no resume semantics). Phase 2 = async/non-blocking toolcalls with resumable frames and merge behavior (opt-in). Phase 3 = SLA/contracts, audit logs, per-token metrics, dedicated capacity guidance.

Kai W. (Eng): Effort estimate: Phase 1 ~2 sprints (small infra changes); Phase 2 ~3-4 sprints (queueing, storage, SDK changes); Phase 3 ~2 sprints + observability/compliance. Unknowns: datastore sizing for paused calls, resume merge complexity, edge-case ordering.

Jake L. (Sales): Need Phase 1 by EoQ to close deal. Can we canary on Dedicated or a partner? Also need contract wording for partial outputs.

Maria P. (Product): Proposed acceptance for Phase 1: 1) Client receives token stream and `call_started` when fncall issued and `call_finished` with result. 2) If webhook slow (eg 5s), system still emits pre-call tokens and `call_started`; no deadlock. 3) Canary on Dedicated at 100 QPS for 24h with <0.1% errors. 4) Request-id and call-id visible in Console logs and via API.

Emma S. (Support): Customer also wants per-request toggle to disable streaming for specific routes and logs showing partial outputs when streaming is on.

Kai W. (Eng): Breaking-change risk: streaming protocol change means SDK bumps and migration docs. Need to decide if `call_started` is public API — recommend public.

Maria P. (Product): Next steps: I'll start a PRD and put phases on roadmap. @Kai W. prepare an architecture short doc (perf, queue/storage needs) before the scoping workshop. @Olivia R. draft customer explainer + example SDK diffs. @Jake L. I'll request legal language for partial outputs and SLA.

Jake L. (Sales): I'll align Acme with the canary timeline and keep them updated.

Emma S. (Support): Attaching customer contact sally@acme.com and ticket ACME-4567. ops-bot: set priority=high.

ops-bot: priority set to high for ticket ACME-4567

Maria P. (Product): Scoping workshop scheduled tomorrow 10:00am. Agenda to follow.

Kai W. (Eng): I'll bring perf numbers and a prototype sketch.

Olivia R. (Solutions Eng): I'll draft example response patterns and a minimal SDK diff today.

Emma S. (Support): Thanks all — will post any customer replies in this thread.
